_about: RAW, VERBATIM record of one real subagent-instrumented benchmark run. Each call was an isolated Claude subagent (tool_uses=0). 'subagent_tokens' is the runtime-reported usage as returned by the harness (NOT author-computed and NOT re-derivable, since it is nondeterministic). Prompts and outputs are stored verbatim so anyone can re-tokenize them with tiktoken (see crosscheck.py) and inspect exactly what was sent and returned. Agent-ids are the runtime trace.
model: Claude (Claude Code subagents, general-purpose). Single model family. n=1.
known_wrinkles: writer_baseline received the document verbatim PLUS condensed (not verbatim) upstream summaries; a true full-transcript baseline would be larger, so the writer-stage TOAP advantage is understated/conservative.
n=1: per-call subagent_tokens is a single nondeterministic sample; small deltas may include noise.
subagent_tokens is one total (prompt+reasoning+output), not split.
judge is the same model family (fresh, blind A/B, no in-context stake).

calls.prompt: Do not use any tools. Do not read files or search anything. Respond directly with exactly one word and nothing else: READY

You are an EXTRACTION agent in a multi-agent pipeline. Do not use any tools. Do not read files or search. Respond directly.

From the incident report below, extract the key structured facts only (trigger, metrics, topology, failure chain, impact, and gaps). Be factual and concise - at most 120 words. Output just the facts, no preamble.

Incident report:
"Incident INC-4821. On March 3 at 14:02 UTC the payments API latency rose from 120ms to 9.4s and the error rate hit 38% for 47 minutes. The trigger was a marketing campaign that drove roughly 5x normal traffic to the checkout endpoint. The payments service runs 4 fixed pods with no autoscaling. The database connection pool (max 20) saturated, causing requests to queue; the queue had no backpressure, so memory grew and 2 pods OOM-restarted, worsening the outage. A manual scale-up to 12 pods at 14:49 restored service. Revenue impact is estimated at 42,000 dollars. The team had load-tested only at 1x expected traffic. No alert fired for connection-pool saturation; the first signal was customer complaints on social media. No deployment occurred, so rollback was not relevant. Proposed action items: (1) enable horizontal autoscaling on the payments service, (2) raise and tune the DB connection pool and add backpressure, (3) add a saturation alert on pool usage, (4) load-test at 5x before campaigns."
calls.output:
Trigger: Marketing campaign drove ~5x normal traffic to the checkout endpoint (INC-4821, March 3, 14:02 UTC).

Metrics: Latency 120ms to 9.4s; error rate 38%; 47-minute duration.

Topology: Payments service on 4 fixed pods, no autoscaling; DB connection pool max 20.

Failure chain: Pool saturated to queue requests; no backpressure to memory growth to 2 pods OOM-restarted to worsened outage. Manual scale-up to 12 pods at 14:49 restored service.

Impact: ~$42,000 revenue loss.

Gaps: Load-tested only at 1x; no connection-pool saturation alert (first signal was social-media complaints); no deployment, so rollback irrelevant.

Root cause: A capacity bottleneck under load. The payments service had no autoscaling (4 fixed pods) and a hard DB connection-pool ceiling (max 20). When the campaign drove 5x traffic, the pool saturated and requests queued without backpressure, causing unbounded memory growth, OOM restarts of 2 pods, and a cascading failure.

Severity: High. Customer-facing checkout was degraded for 47 minutes (38% errors, 9.4s latency) with ~$42,000 direct revenue loss.

Prevention: Autoscaling on the payments service; load testing at realistic peak multiples (not just 1x) to expose pool limits; bounded queues with backpressure and request shedding; right-sized pool plus a connection-pool saturation alert so detection beats social-media complaints. Coordinating capacity planning with marketing on known traffic spikes would also have helped.
